content: {"summary":"The evidence shows that during the 15 May 2025 incident the edge gateway returned 504 errors as cache misses and writes were blocked, and the catalog‑api pods logged QueuePool timeouts because their SQLAlchemy connection pool (10 base connections + 5 overflow, max 30) drained quickly when requests stalled, exhausting the limited pool.","likely_cause":"Exhaustion of the catalog‑api SQLAlchemy connection pool (max 30 sessions) caused by stalled requests, leading to QueuePool timeouts and edge‑gateway 504 errors","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"Edge‑gateway began answering 504 errors as cache misses and writes were blocked","evidence_ids":["INC-0042#0"],"quote":"edge-gateway began answering 504"},{"text":"The pool drained almost immediately and pods logged QueuePool timeouts","evidence_ids":["INC-0042#1"],"quote":"pool drained almost immediately... logging QueuePool timeouts"},{"text":"Catalog‑api pods use a SQLAlchemy pool of 10 connections plus 5 overflow, max 30 sessions","evidence_ids":["RB-028#1"],"quote":"SQLAlchemy pool allows 10 connections plus 5 overflow, so at most 30 sessions"}],"next_checks":["Check the May 2025 deployment changelog for any changes to the SQLAlchemy pool size or async worker configuration","Verify if the connection‑pool settings were altered in that release","Examine request‑latency and connection‑usage metrics during the incident window","Confirm whether cache‑layer settings were modified in the same deployment"]}
